transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, yeah… thanks for seeing me. I guess the main thing is people keep telling me I’m not really listening. Like my supervisor at work, or my wife, they’ll be talking right to me, and then a minute later I realize I only caught maybe half of what they said. Then I have to ask them to repeat it, which… I know can be frustrating. I’m not trying to ignore anybody or anything.
Do you think you’re having trouble hearing what people say?

I don’t think it’s my hearing, no. I mean, I can hear people fine most of the time… it’s more like I realize afterward I didn’t really take in what they said. If that makes sense. But I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.
When someone is talking to you, do you find your mind drifting off?

Yeah… I think that’s probably a fair way to put it. I mean, I don’t mean to drift off, and I’m not trying to be rude, but someone—like my supervisor or my wife—can be talking right to me, and then a minute later I realize I only really caught part of it. Then I’m asking them to say it again, which I know gets old for them.
Looking back, were you already having this kind of trouble paying attention when you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to blame everything on school or make it sound like I was a terrible kid, but looking back, I was kind of always like this.

Teachers moved my seat a lot because I couldn’t really stay put, and I’d call out answers before I was supposed to. I remember getting in trouble for butting into other kids’ work too, like trying to jump in or tell them what to do. That was before middle school, so… yeah, I guess it’s been there a long time.
Besides work, does this cause problems for you at home, too?

Yeah… I mean, I wish I could say it’s only at work, but no, it does show up at home too.

I try to help, I really do, but sometimes I end up throwing off the routine more than helping it. My wife gets frustrated, and the kids do too, because I’ll interrupt or rush things or mess up the flow of what we’re supposed to be doing.

And… I guess at work it’s been more serious than I like to admit. I’ve had formal warnings, and I do worry sometimes that if I don’t get a handle on it, I could lose my job or, worse, cause a safety problem on the line. I don’t want to sound dramatic, but that’s honestly a concern.
Do you spend a lot of your day worrying about things?

I don’t think so… not a lot of the day, anyway. I mean, I worry about normal stuff—work, bills, whether I’m doing right by my family—but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around consumed by worry all day.

At least, I don’t think that’s the main thing. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed any trouble hearing people, especially when there’s background noise?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, if there’s a lot going on around me I might miss something, but I haven’t really noticed it as a hearing problem.

I guess I’ve always figured it was more me not catching it or being distracted, not that I couldn’t hear them. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Not really, no. I mean… I get frustrated with myself sometimes, and I have rough days, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling depressed.

At least not in the way I think you mean. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Have you been having trouble with your memory?

I don’t think so, not in a serious way. I mean, I forget little things sometimes—like anyone does—but I haven’t really thought of it as a memory problem.

Is that what you mean, like forgetting appointments or conversations?
Have you had trouble finding the right words when you speak?

Not that I’ve really noticed, no. I mean, sometimes I might stumble over what I’m trying to say, but I wouldn’t say I’m having trouble finding words exactly.

I can usually get my point across, I think. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder with onset in childhood and persistent symptoms into adulthood. The patient confirms current inattentive symptoms (not taking in what others say, distractibility/mind drifting) and childhood/current hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (could not stay seated, calling out answers, intruding on others, interrupting/rushing things). Symptoms are present across work and home settings and cause clear functional impairment, including formal work warnings and family conflict. Anxiety, depression, hearing difficulty, memory disorder, and language problems were not supported as primary explanations.
